title: Edit a response in the right order
instructions: The prompt asks: ‘Write about something you learned at school that you used in another area of your life. Explain what you did and what you learned from the experience.’ Use only these verified notes: in science class, Mira learned that a fair comparison changes one variable while keeping other conditions alike; at home, eight basil seedlings in identical pots were wilting; she placed four seedlings where they received morning sun and four where they received afternoon sun; she kept the soil, pot size and amount of water alike; for ten days, she checked leaf firmness at 7 p.m.; by day ten, three of the four morning-sun seedlings had firm leaves, compared with one of the four afternoon-sun seedlings; the small observation did not prove what would happen to every basil plant. The flawed draft mentions the science lesson, describes the classroom walls, gives the day-ten figures before explaining the home procedure, calls the result ‘proof for all plants’, and ends without explaining what Mira learned. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which problem should Mira repair FIRST?

options.text: The draft has not yet explained what Mira learned from applying the school method.
One sentence uses a comma where a full stop could be used.
The word ‘seedling’ is misspelled once.
Two sentences begin with the word ‘I’.

choice_rationales.A: The prompt explicitly requires the learning from the experience, so this is a task-fulfilment gap.
choice_rationales.B: Punctuation matters, but it comes after the response contains every required idea.
choice_rationales.C: Spelling is a convention-level correction and cannot fill the missing reflection.
choice_rationales.D: Repeated openings may be improved later, but they are not the main failure described.

parts.hint: Compare the draft with every command in the prompt before looking at individual words.
parts.correct_explanation: A missing required reflection threatens task fulfilment and therefore outranks sentence-level or convention-level corrections.

parts.prompt: Which focus sentence would best keep the response centred on the prompt?

options.text: Science is a subject with many experiments, colourful diagrams and difficult words.
The fair-testing method I learned in science helped me investigate why our basil seedlings were wilting at home.
Basil is certainly the best herb for every family to grow.
My classroom walls were pale green, although the laboratory tables were grey.

choice_rationales.A: This describes the subject generally but does not establish the transfer to another area of life.
choice_rationales.B: It names the school learning, its use at home and the problem that will organise the response.
choice_rationales.C: The notes do not support a universal judgement about basil.
choice_rationales.D: The colours do not advance the response's controlling focus.

parts.hint: The focus should connect the school learning directly to its use outside school.
parts.correct_explanation: A useful focus sentence fulfils the transfer requirement and gives the later procedure and reflection a clear purpose.

parts.prompt: Which order gives the reader the clearest route through the response?

options.text: Day-ten figures → classroom wall colours → home problem → fair-testing method → reflection
Home problem → relevant school method → controlled home comparison → bounded result → reflection
Reflection → spelling corrections → day-ten figures → unrelated classroom description → home problem
Classroom wall colours → universal claim → home problem → day-ten figures → school method

choice_rationales.A: The result arrives before the reader understands the comparison, and an irrelevant detail interrupts the route.
choice_rationales.B: Each stage prepares for the next: problem, transferable method, application, observed result and meaning.
choice_rationales.C: Surface correction is not a paragraph job, and the evidence appears without a logical setup.
choice_rationales.D: The response opens with irrelevant material and makes an unsupported claim before explaining the method.

parts.hint: Choose the order in which each paragraph answers the reader's next likely question.
parts.correct_explanation: A reverse outline should reveal a continuous route from the real-life problem to the method, evidence and reflection.

parts.prompt: Which sentence should be deleted because it has no useful job in this response?

options.text: In science, I learned to change one variable while keeping other conditions alike.
Our classroom walls were pale green, and the laboratory tables were grey.
I kept the pot size, soil and amount of water alike for both groups.
The small comparison taught me to test a possible explanation systematically instead of relying on a guess.

choice_rationales.A: This identifies the transferable school learning required by the prompt.
choice_rationales.B: The colours neither explain the fair-test method nor develop its application or significance.
choice_rationales.C: This is essential evidence that the home comparison applied the school method.
choice_rationales.D: This supplies the reflection required by the task and explains why the experience mattered.

parts.hint: Ask what each sentence contributes to the focus, application, result or reflection.
parts.correct_explanation: Accurate detail is still removable when it does not perform a relevant job in the response.

parts.prompt: Which TWO changes are convention-level corrections that should be made only after the task, order and development are secure?

options.text: Add the missing reflection on what Mira learned.
Move the procedure before the day-ten result.
Correct ‘seedling were’ to ‘seedlings were’.
Replace a comma splice with a full stop.
Remove the unsupported claim that the observation proves what happens to every basil plant.

choice_rationales.A: This is a task-fulfilment and development revision.
choice_rationales.C: This repairs number agreement at the sentence surface.
choice_rationales.D: This repairs a punctuation and sentence-boundary fault.
choice_rationales.E: This is an evidence-scope revision that protects the meaning of the response.

parts.hint: Select the changes that repair grammar or punctuation without changing the response's ideas or route.
parts.correct_explanation: Agreement and punctuation belong to the final convention pass; task, organisation and evidence-scope repairs come earlier.

parts.prompt: Which revised paragraph best reflects all four editing passes while staying within the verified notes?

options.text: Science is very useful. Our walls were green and I like basil. The experiment proved that morning sun always saves every plant, so everyone should follow my method.

The fair-testing method I learned in science helped me investigate why eight basil seedlings were wilting at home. I placed four in morning sun and four in afternoon sun while keeping their pots, soil and water alike. For ten days, I checked leaf firmness at the same time each evening. By day ten, three morning-sun seedlings had firm leaves, compared with one afternoon-sun seedling. This small comparison did not prove what would happen to every basil plant, but it taught me to test one possible explanation systematically instead of relying on a guess.
By day ten there were three and one. Science had experiments. The seedling were checked, I moved them and this proves everything about sunlight.
I learned fair testing. Moreover, basil. Furthermore, the classroom was attractive. In conclusion, the result was successful and perfect.

choice_rationales.A: It retains irrelevant material and expands a small observation into an unsupported universal claim.
choice_rationales.B: It answers the transfer task, follows a clear route, develops the comparison, bounds the result and controls its sentences and conventions.
choice_rationales.C: The evidence lacks context, agreement and sentence boundaries, while the final claim exceeds the notes.
choice_rationales.D: Decorative connectors cannot replace procedure, evidence or reflection, and ‘perfect’ is unsupported.

parts.hint: Choose the version that fulfils the prompt, orders the method before the result, explains the learning and preserves the evidence limit.
parts.correct_explanation: Effective editing protects the response at every level: task, organisation, development, sentence control and conventions.
